verdicts.rewritten_summary: Alchetron mirror of the territory's LGBT-rights page (updated 25 Apr 2026): same-sex sexual activity legal; discrimination protections in force since 2009; same-sex marriage legal on Ascension Island since 2017 — the marriage-law jurisdiction of the territory.

GayLawNet laws index for the territory (page accessed 23 Jun 2013, citing ILGA State-sponsored Homophobia): consensual same-sex relations became lawful in 2001 and the age of consent is equalised at 16 territory-wide; page frames the territory as an Overseas Country or Territory of the EU (Charter applicability).

adds.title: Human Dignity Trust country profile: Solomon Islands (via Wayback snapshot)
adds.summary: Human Dignity Trust profile: Solomon Islands criminalises same-sex sexual activity between men and between women, maximum penalty 14 years' imprisonment (Penal Code provisions); the profile documents the colonial-law basis and the absence of recorded prosecutions in recent years.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Solomon Islands (Wikipedia summary API)
adds.summary: Wikipedia reference summary: male and female same-sex sexual activity is illegal and punishable by up to 14 years' imprisonment, but the law is not enforced; LGBTQ people face legal challenges not experienced by other residents, with no relationship recognition or non-discrimination shield.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: GlobalGayz news archive for Sierra Leone (Richard Ammon, items dated 2004-2010): records the November 2004 rape and murder of lesbian activist FannyAnn Eddy, the January 2005 arrest of her killer, police refusal to classify it as a hate crime, and the alleged murderer's reported escape from custody in July 2005 — dated evidence on violence against LGBT activists and the justice response.

Foreign Policy (9 Mar 2020, Anna-Catherine Brigida): prosecution of the death of Camila Díaz Córdova, a transgender Salvadoran woman, as a hate crime — activists called it an advance toward El Salvador's first hate-crime homicide conviction while documenting continuing discrimination and abuse of LGBTQ citizens.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Dilemas journal article (Arévalo et al., Fundação Oswaldo Cruz, 2024): 'Denied deaths' builds a profile of crimes, victims and perpetrators of homicides against LGBTI+ people in El Salvador across 2000-2020 — the peer-reviewed longitudinal dataset on anti-LGBTI+ killings for the period.

HRW report 'Every Day I Live in Fear' (7 Oct 2020): El Salvador (with Guatemala and Honduras) fails to effectively address violence and entrenched discrimination against LGBT people, driving asylum claims to the US; documents obstacles to obtaining protection.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: HRW (31 Jul 2020): San Salvador judge found three police officers guilty of the January 2019 killing of transgender woman Camila Díaz Córdova and sentenced each to 20 years; the 28 July 2020 judgment is the first homicide conviction in El Salvador for killing a transgender person, hailed by HRW as pivotal for transgender Salvadorans' rights.

Washington Blade (9 Sep 2015): National Assembly approved legal-code reforms so killings motivated by sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, political affiliation or gender draw 30-60 years under Article 129 — the enhanced hate-crime penalty framework on the books since.

ILGA-Europe Rainbow Map, Legal gender recognition category (2026 edition): San Marino is listed among the countries where there is NO functioning legal or administrative process for legal gender recognition.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Euronews (4 Jun 2019): citizens voted by referendum to insert a clause prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation into the constitution of San Marino — the motion passed.

The Guardian (4 Apr 2022): Paolo Rondelli appointed captain regent — the world's first openly gay head of state (six-month term, no executive power); the article notes homosexuality was punishable by jail time in San Marino until 2004 and legal recognition of gay couples followed in 2016.
Euronews Italia (16 Nov 2018): San Marino's legislature approved a civil-unions law, described as 'leaner than the Cirinnà' Italian statute — the relationship-recognition framework in force.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (16 Feb 2016) on Benjamin Christman's 'Report on the Treatment of Gay Persons in Somalia' (published 2 Feb 2016): evidence that gay persons should not be returned to Somalia due to persecution risk, supporting refugee-status claims; notes Somalia's anti-homosexuality law provides up to... [report excerpt] — non-refoulement basis for LGBT asylum seekers.

Al Jazeera (Jul 2013) 'Gay Somali refugees face death threats': refugees in Kenya face threats and racist discrimination, with Al-Shabaab publicising intent to 'enforce harsh punishments' against homosexuality and senior figures claiming a 'death chamber' for gay and lesbians if returned; UN officials nevertheless pushed return — dated account of persecution driving displacement.

Balkan Insight (27 Feb 2024): Serbian authorities investigating allegations that police officers assaulted two LGBT people — a probe into police violence against LGBT citizens (outcome: investigation opened).
Da se zna! (2 Sep 2025): presentation of the association's 8th annual hate-crime report, 'Transphobia and Homophobia in Serbia 2024' — the standing civil-society incident register for the year.

APT (Association for the Prevention of Torture) Serbia country page, national-preventive-mechanism recommendations: the Penal and Correctional Institution in Padinska Skela, Belgrade, shall let transgender women at intake choose a female officer for searches/body inspection rather than a male or combined search — a concrete custodial-rights finding for trans detainees.

HRW World Report 2025 (Serbia/Kosovo chapter): intolerance and violence against LGBT people remained significant concerns in Serbia in 2024; state response to July-August protests (activist arrests, smear campaigns) highlighted rule-of-law weaknesses.
